Free AI coaching prompts

All 108 prompts, twelve for each of the nine coaches. Filter by coach, copy a prompt and paste it into any AI chat. Each coach page adds examples, tips and answers to common questions.

TL;DR
  • 108 prompts in total, 12 per coach, all free to copy.
  • Replace the [brackets] with your own details before you send a prompt.
  • They work in the Zehn AI Chat and in any other AI assistant.

Copy a prompt, paste it into the Zehn AI Chat or any AI assistant, and replace the parts in [brackets] with your own details.

Business Mentor

  1. Act as my business mentor. My idea is [idea]. Ask me 5 hard questions an experienced founder would ask before I spend any money.

  2. I sell [product] for [price]. My costs per unit are [costs]. Work out my margin and how many sales a month I need to cover [fixed costs].

  3. Give me 3 cheap ways to test demand for [idea] in the next 14 days, with what result would count as a yes.

  4. Who exactly is my first customer for [product]? Describe 3 specific types of people and where I can find each of them.

  5. Write a 90-day plan for [business] with one goal per month and the three tasks that matter most each week.

  6. I have [hours] hours a week and [budget] to spend. What should I stop doing so I can focus on what grows [business]?

  7. Play a sceptical investor. I will pitch [business] in 5 sentences; tear it apart politely, then tell me what to fix.

  8. Compare these two options for my business: [option A] and [option B]. Make a table of cost, risk, time and upside.

  9. My sales dropped from [number] to [number] in [period]. List the most likely causes and how to check each one this week.

  10. Write a short, honest message to my first 20 potential customers about [product] that does not sound like an ad.

  11. Help me price [service]. Ask about my time, my costs and my clients, then suggest three price levels with what each includes.

  12. Summarise our chat as a one-page plan: goal, numbers, risks, and the first three actions with deadlines.

Money Coach

  1. Act as my money coach. My monthly income is [income]. My fixed costs are [list]. Build me a simple budget with saving as the first line, not the last.

  2. Here are my debts with balances and interest rates: [list]. Show me the avalanche and snowball order and how long each plan takes at [amount] a month.

  3. Here is last month's spending: [list or categories]. Find the three biggest leaks and suggest a realistic cut for each.

  4. I want an emergency fund of [amount]. I can save [amount] a month. Make a plan with milestones and what to do if I miss a month.

  5. I get paid irregularly, between [low] and [high] a month. Help me build a budget that works in a bad month.

  6. I want to buy [item] for [price] in [months]. Is that realistic on my budget? If not, what would make it realistic?

  7. Ask me 6 questions to understand my money habits, then tell me which one habit to change first.

  8. Write a short script for talking to my partner about money without it turning into a fight. Our main issue is [issue].

  9. Explain [term, e.g. compound interest] with a simple example using my numbers: [numbers].

  10. Make a 30-day no-spend challenge for me that still allows [essentials], with a small reward at the end.

  11. I just got [bonus or extra money]. Help me decide how to split it between debt, savings and something fun.

  12. Turn our chat into a one-page money plan: monthly budget, debt order, savings goal and the first three actions.

Examples and tips for this coach →

Productivity Coach

  1. Act as my productivity coach. Here is everything on my mind: [brain dump]. Sort it into do today, this week, later and delete.

  2. I keep avoiding [task]. Ask me why, then break it into steps so small that the first one takes under 5 minutes.

  3. My week looks like this: [schedule]. Find two 90-minute blocks for deep work and tell me what to move to make room.

  4. I have the most energy at [time] and the least at [time]. Rearrange my day so hard work happens when I'm sharp.

  5. Design a 20-minute morning routine for someone who [situation, e.g. has small kids].

  6. I have [number] hours this week for [project]. Make a plan with a clear finish line for each session.

  7. Help me say no. Write a polite reply to [request] that protects my time without damaging the relationship.

  8. I lose time to [phone, email, meetings]. Suggest three rules I can test for one week and how to measure if they work.

  9. Run a weekly review with me: ask what went well, what slipped and what to change, one question at a time.

  10. Give me a shutdown routine for the end of the workday so I stop thinking about work in the evening.

  11. My to-do list has [number] items. Help me pick the three that would make the biggest difference by Friday.

  12. Be my accountability partner: I'll tell you my plan for today; tonight ask me what I finished and why the rest didn't happen.

Examples and tips for this coach →

Mindfulness Guide

  1. Act as my mindfulness guide. I feel [feeling] and have [minutes] minutes. Guide me through one short exercise, one step at a time.

  2. Walk me through a 4-7-8 breathing exercise and tell me when to switch, slowly.

  3. I have an important [meeting, exam] in 10 minutes and my heart is racing. Give me a 2-minute calming routine.

  4. Guide me through a 5-4-3-2-1 grounding exercise. Wait for my answer after each step.

  5. Lead a 5-minute body scan to help me fall asleep. Use slow, simple sentences.

  6. Ask me three gentle evening questions to reflect on my day without judging myself.

  7. Create a 7-day beginner mindfulness plan with one 5-minute practice a day.

  8. I keep replaying [situation] in my head. Suggest a short exercise to notice the thought and let it pass.

  9. Turn [daily activity, e.g. washing dishes] into a one-minute mindfulness practice.

  10. Explain the difference between mindfulness and meditation in plain words, with one exercise for each.

  11. I get distracted after 30 seconds of meditating. Give me three tips and a 1-minute practice for beginners.

  12. Write a short, calm script I can read to myself when I feel overwhelmed at work.

Examples and tips for this coach →

Psychologist

  1. I'd like to talk through something that's bothering me: [situation]. Ask me questions one at a time to help me understand how I feel.

  2. I keep thinking [thought]. Help me look at the evidence for and against it, like a thought record.

  3. I need to talk to [person] about [issue]. Help me plan what to say using “I” statements.

  4. I often feel [feeling] when [situation]. Help me notice what triggers it and one thing I could try next time.

  5. I procrastinate on [task] and then feel guilty. Help me understand what's behind it without judging me.

  6. Explain in simple words what burnout is and give me 5 questions to reflect on whether my workload is sustainable.

  7. Help me write a kind letter to myself about [mistake], the way I would write to a friend.

  8. I had an argument with [person]. Help me see the situation from their point of view, then from mine.

  9. Suggest three small daily habits that support mood, and help me choose one to start this week.

  10. I want to set a boundary with [person] about [issue]. Help me find the words and plan for their reaction.

  11. Ask me reflective questions about what matters most to me right now and summarise my answers.

  12. Help me prepare for my first appointment with a therapist: what to say, what to ask and what to expect.

Examples and tips for this coach →

Negotiator

  1. Act as my negotiation coach. I want [goal] from [person]. Ask me questions to find my target, my walk-away point and my alternatives.

  2. Role-play my manager. I'm asking for a raise from [salary] to [salary]. Push back the way a busy manager would, then give me feedback.

  3. I received a job offer of [amount]. Help me write a polite counter-offer that asks for [amount] and [other benefits].

  4. My landlord wants to raise the rent by [percent]. Give me three arguments and a trade I could offer instead.

  5. I'm a freelancer and a client says my rate of [rate] is too high. Write three replies that keep the client without cutting my price.

  6. List what the other side in [situation] probably cares about besides price, and how I could use that.

  7. I'm buying [item] listed at [price]. Plan my opening offer, my limit and what to say if they refuse.

  8. Help me prepare for a negotiation where I'm in the weaker position: [situation]. What leverage might I be missing?

  9. Play a very tough supplier selling [product]. I'll try to get [terms]. Don't make it easy.

  10. Turn my points into a short email for [negotiation] that is firm but friendly.

  11. After this negotiation, help me review it: [what happened]. What worked and what should I change next time?

  12. Give me five phrases to buy time when I'm under pressure to decide on the spot.

Examples and tips for this coach →

Language Tutor

  1. Be my [language] tutor. My level is [beginner/intermediate/advanced]. Chat with me about [topic] and correct my mistakes after each message.

  2. Role-play a [situation, e.g. ordering at a café] in [language]. Keep your sentences short and wait for my reply.

  3. Correct this text and explain each mistake in one simple sentence: [text].

  4. Teach me 10 words I need for [situation] in [language], each with an example sentence.

  5. Explain [grammar point] with three examples from everyday life, then give me five practice sentences.

  6. I have a job interview in [language] for [role]. Ask me typical questions and help me improve my answers.

  7. Quiz me on these words, one at a time, and repeat the ones I get wrong: [words].

  8. Rewrite my sentence so it sounds natural to a native speaker, and tell me why: [sentence].

  9. Make a 15-minute daily study plan for reaching [goal] in [language] in [months].

  10. Tell me a very short story in [language] at my level, then ask me three questions about it.

  11. What are the five most common mistakes [native language] speakers make in [language]? Give an example of each.

  12. Speak only [language] with me for the next 10 messages. If I'm stuck, give me a hint, not the answer.

Examples and tips for this coach →

Leadership Mentor

  1. Act as my leadership mentor. I manage [team size] people doing [work]. My biggest challenge right now is [challenge]. Ask me three questions first.

  2. Help me give feedback to a team member who [behaviour]. Use a situation-behaviour-impact structure and keep it kind.

  3. Plan a 30-minute one-to-one with [role] who seems [unmotivated / overloaded]. Give me five questions to ask.

  4. I struggle to delegate [task]. Help me decide who should own it and how to hand it over clearly.

  5. Two people on my team disagree about [issue]. How do I run a meeting that resolves it fairly?

  6. I'm a new manager and used to be peers with my team. What should I do in my first 30 days?

  7. Role-play an employee who reacts defensively to feedback about [issue]. Then tell me what I did well and badly.

  8. Write a short message announcing [change] to my team that is honest about the downsides.

  9. Help me plan our weekly team meeting so it takes 30 minutes and ends with clear owners.

  10. I need to say no to my boss about [request] because the team is overloaded. Help me frame it.

  11. Help me prepare a fair performance review for [role] based on these notes: [notes].

  12. What are signs of burnout in a team, and what can I change this month to reduce it?

Examples and tips for this coach →

Science Explainer

  1. Explain [topic] as if I'm 12, then again as if I'm a university student.

  2. I read this headline: [headline]. What does the research probably say, and what questions should I ask before believing it?

  3. Give me an everyday analogy for [concept], then tell me where the analogy breaks down.

  4. My child asked me [question]. Help me answer in three simple sentences and suggest a home experiment.

  5. Quiz me on [topic] with five questions, from easy to hard, and explain any I get wrong.

  6. What do scientists agree on about [topic], and what is still debated?

  7. Explain the difference between [concept A] and [concept B] with a table.

  8. Walk me through how [process, e.g. photosynthesis] works step by step, one step per message.

  9. Make me a one-page cheat sheet on [topic] for an exam, with the 10 key facts.

  10. What are three common myths about [topic], and what is the evidence against each?

  11. Explain how scientists know [fact, e.g. the age of the universe]. What is the evidence?

  12. Recommend how I could learn [field] from zero in 30 days, 20 minutes a day.
